cw-flight-deck.text: RFV Crimson Warden primary flight deck — enormous industrial carrier deck with two main launch lanes, a central service spine, recessed tie-downs, aircraft elevators, emergency barriers and a separate recovery track feeding aft. Deep Fleet blue structural ribs, Ion White safety markings, dark nonreflective deck surface and restrained ember-crimson lane identifiers. Busy, loud and practical.

cw-ready-room.text: Crimson Warden squadron ready room — compact tiered seats, mission wall, helmet racks, hydration station and scarred table surfaces. Fleet blue/white with small crimson squadron marks, personal mugs and taped maintenance notes; no ceremonial decor.

cw-bridge.text: Crimson Warden bridge — broad carrier command space built around navigation, tactical, operations and damage-control stations rather than a single throne-like command chair. Forward display wall shows corridor beacons, convoy tracks and carrier launch/recovery geometry.

cw-flight-ops.text: Crimson Warden flight-operations center — enclosed coordination room overlooking the flight deck through armored transparent panels and sensor feeds. Launch boards, fuel clocks, recovery queue and maintenance-state displays are always visible.

cw-maintenance.text: Crimson Warden maintenance bay — dense hangar of partially opened fighters, lift frames, parts cages, diagnostic carts, stripped panels and mechanics working around hot machinery. Every aircraft should carry visible status tags and incomplete repairs.

cw-medical.text: Crimson Warden medical bay — efficient Fleet trauma space with flight-medicine stations, compact surgical capability, suit-cutting tools and expandable triage lanes. Ion White task light over dark blue deck surfaces; practical rather than pristine.

cw-berthing.text: Crimson Warden pilot and crew berthing — narrow bunks, lockers, drying racks, charging points and improvised personal objects. The carrier's scale disappears here; it feels cramped, ordinary and lived in.

cw-recovery-craft.text: Crimson Warden recovery craft cockpit and lock — blunt utility craft with wide rescue windows, manipulator controls, tether reels, two crash couches and a rear pressure lock. High-visibility rescue markings are practical, not heroic.

cw-damage-control.text: Crimson Warden damage-control passage — armored service corridor near the flight-deck pressure boundary, with isolation doors, fire mains, cable trunks, patch lockers and emergency lighting. Geography must stay consistent when pressure and fire damage spread.

convoy-zone.text: Verge relief convoy emergency volume — damaged freighters and passenger transports clustered near a line of green safety beacons, cargo and hull fragments drifting toward the unsafe edge. Crimson Warden holds farther coreward as its fighters, rescue craft and tugs move between civilian ships.
